title: Faculty.Professor.Associate - Full-Time
description:
Faculty.Professor.Associate - Full-Time

Med-Psychiatry - Pennsylvania-Pittsburgh - (26006672)

**Associate Professor of Psychiatry (with Tenure)**  
University of Pittsburgh, Department of Psychiatry  
Pittsburgh, United States

**Job Description**  
The Department of Psychiatry at the University of Pittsburgh is seeking a full-time Associate Professor with tenure to lead and advance innovative research in psychiatric illness and mental health. We seek an accomplished investigator with an established, externally funded research program and a strong record of scholarly achievement.

The successful candidate will:  

* Lead an independent and nationally recognized research program focused on the neurobiological substrates of complex human cognitive functions and the mechanisms underlying cognitive dysfunction.
* Develop and direct innovative research initiatives that advance scientific knowledge and contribute to the Department's research mission.
* Secure and maintain extramural research funding as a principal investigator.
* Publish high-impact research findings in peer-reviewed journals and present scholarly work at national and international conferences.
* Provide scientific leadership within a highly collaborative and multidisciplinary research environment.
* Mentor graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, junior faculty, and other trainees in their professional development and research activities.
* Contribute to departmental, university, and professional service activities.
* Ensure all research activities are conducted in accordance with university, federal, and other applicable guidelines governing the responsible conduct of research.

The search committee will primarily be looking for:  

* A sustained record of scholarly accomplishment and impactful peer-reviewed publications.
* A history of successful extramural funding as a principal investigator.
* Evidence of national or international recognition in the candidate's field of research.
* Demonstrated leadership in interdisciplinary and collaborative research initiatives.
* Excellence in mentoring trainees, junior faculty, and research staff.
* A commitment to advancing a collaborative and inclusive academic research environment.

Successful candidates will join a vibrant and highly interactive research community with a long history of excellence in basic and translational neuroscience research.

**Qualifications**  

* PhD, MD, MD/PhD, or equivalent doctoral degree in Neuroscience, Psychology, Psychiatry, or a related field.
* Qualifications consistent with appointment at the rank of Associate Professor with tenure at the University of Pittsburgh.
* An established and externally funded research program relevant to psychiatry, neuroscience, or mental health research.
* A strong and sustained record of peer-reviewed publications and scholarly impact.
* Evidence of scientific leadership and national or international recognition in the field.
* Demonstrated excellence in mentoring and training students, postdoctoral fellows, junior investigators, and research staff.
* Strong organizational, leadership, and collaborative skills.
* Ability to contribute to the Department's research, educational, and service missions.

**About the Employer**  
At the University of Pittsburgh Department of Psychiatry, we excel in our mission to:  

* Provide superb behavioral health services to our patients and their families;
* Pursue the development of improved diagnostic techniques and therapeutic interventions through innovative research;
* Provide a stimulating learning environment for medical and graduate students, residents, psychology interns, and postdoctoral fellows.

Our success in each of these areas depends on a highly interactive community of clinicians, scientists, and educators who bring diversity in background, experience, expertise, and perspective to our mission.

An essential partner in this work is UPMC Western Psychiatric Hospital, a national leader in innovative treatment of mental health and addiction disorders. Pitt Psychiatry's faculty of more than 230 members across basic and clinical science disciplines is central to our success in advancing research, education, and clinical care.

**Areas of Research**  

* Psychology
* Psychiatry
* Neuroscience

**How to Apply**  
Please apply by going to our job site (https://cfopitt.taleo.net/careersection/pitt\_faculty\_external/jobsearch.ftl), searching job code 26006672 in the keyword search, and submitting your materials through our Pitt system.

title: Post Doctoral Associate - Dr. Omar El Gharbawie's Laboratory
description:
Post Doctoral Associate - Dr. Omar El Gharbawie's Laboratory

Med-Neurobiology - Pennsylvania-Pittsburgh - (26006732)

**Postdoctoral Position in Systems Neuroscience: Sensorimotor Circuits in Non-Human Primates** **(University of Pittsburgh)**

A fully funded postdoctoral position is available in the laboratory of Dr. Omar Gharbawie at the University of Pittsburgh. We study the structural and functional organization of brain circuits underlying sensorimotor control and cognition. Our lab also seeks to understand the neural basis of resting state networks. Our investigations use awake/behaving monkeys that are trained to perform manual tasks or studied during rest.

Our approach combines complementary methods across scales:

* **Recording:** high-density electrophysiology, intrinsic signal optical imaging, and fMRI
* **Causal manipulation:** microstimulation, optogenetics, and pharmacological inactivation
* **Anatomy:** tract tracing, cytoarchitectonics, spatial transcriptomics, and MRI

The postdoctoral fellow will lead research projects using several of these methods, with the opportunity to shape new directions in the lab. Collaboration and teamwork are central to our work.

**Training environment**  
Our lab is housed in the Systems Neuroscience Center at the University of Pittsburgh. Lab members have access to resources through the School of Medicine, School of Engineering, and the Center for the Neural Basis of Cognition (CNBC), which is joint between Pitt and Carnegie Mellon University. Pittsburgh is one of the strongest hubs for primate neuroscience, with 27 active research groups, most within walking distance of each other. The community offers extensive training and professional development opportunities including grant writing and career planning. Postdocs are strongly encouraged to engage with our weekly seminars, distinguished lecture series, and neuroscience-related workshops.

**Qualifications**

* PhD in neuroscience, engineering, computer science, or a related field by the start of the appointment
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Preferred: experience with electrophysiology, optical imaging, fMRI, psychophysics, *in vivo* animal work, or neural data analysis. Candidates strong in one area (including computational backgrounds) are encouraged to apply; we will provide training in the others.

The position is fully supported by NIH funding awarded to the lab. The stipend is competitive and commensurate with experience and accomplishments, following NIH postdoctoral guidelines. Health insurance and other benefits are provided.

Please email Dr. Gharbawie at omar@pitt.edu with the subject line "Postdoc application" and include:  
1. Curriculum vitae  
2. A statement (1–2 pages) describing your previous research, interests for postdoctoral work, and career goals  
3. Names and contact information for three references (we will contact references only for finalists)

title: Faculty.Professor.Research Assistant - Full-Time
description:
Faculty.Professor.Research Assistant - Full-Time

Med-Neurological Surgery - Pennsylvania-Pittsburgh - (26006115)

The University of Pittsburgh Department of Neurological Surgery, Abel Lab (TENOR Lab), seeks a Research Assistant Professor- Human Intracranial Electrophysiology, to help manage the electrophysiology arm of an active, grant-funded research program in human auditory neuroscience and pediatric epilepsy. The lab uses intracranial EEG (iEEG) recordings from patients undergoing epilepsy surgery to study the cortical organization of auditory processing, voice perception, categorical encoding, and the development of functional networks across childhood and adolescence.

This is a faculty-level research position for a scientist ready to assist with the lab's electrophysiology operations, contribute intellectually to its scientific direction, and oversee the lab’s operations. The successful candidate will work closely with the PI with the experimental infrastructure, data pipelines, and trainee supervision. The expectation is to assist with regular publications in high level journals. Responsibilities include assist with grant writing and scientific development, data collection and management, mentoring and supervision, operational leadership of the electrophysiology program.

This is a full-time, non-tenure-track faculty appointment. Rank and salary commensurate with experience and qualifications.

Minimum Qualifications to be considered for this position: PhD, MD, or MD/PhD in neuroscience, bioengineering, neural engineering, or a closely related field. Demonstrated research experience in human or animal electrophysiology, with a record of contributions to peer-reviewed publications. Strong quantitative and programming skills (e.g., MATLAB, Python) for neural signal processing and analysis. Evidence of scientific writing ability, including contributions to grants and/or manuscripts. Demonstrated ability to work effectively within an interdisciplinary team spanning basic science and clinical environments.

Interested candidates, please go to Home | Talent Center: Careers at Pitt | University of Pittsburgh and use requisition #26006115 to apply for this position.
